stem.en: An organ must contract rhythmically all through a person's life, without conscious control and without getting tired. Which kind of muscle tissue does this?

text.en: Skeletal muscle, because it can make the strongest pull of the three kinds.

feedback.en: No. Skeletal muscle makes voluntary movements, under your control. The muscle described here works without conscious control.

text.en: Cardiac muscle, whose branched fibres contract rhythmically without tiring.

feedback.en: Yes. Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart, and it works rhythmically throughout life without fatigue.

text.en: Smooth muscle, because it lines the walls of hollow organs such as the intestine.

feedback.en: No. Smooth muscle is involuntary, but it makes slow, continuous movements such as digestion, not the lifelong rhythm of a heartbeat.

text.en: Skeletal and smooth muscle taking turns, so that each one can rest in between.

feedback.en: No. The heart has its own muscle, cardiac muscle, which does not need to take turns with any other muscle.

explanation.en: The organ needs three things at once: rhythmic contraction, no conscious control, and no tiring over a lifetime. Cardiac muscle has all three, which is why the heart can beat throughout life without fatigue. Skeletal muscle is voluntary, and smooth muscle makes slow, continuous movements rather than a heartbeat.

hints.en: List the three needs, then test each kind of muscle against all three.
Which muscle is found only in the heart?
